Hi Anita / Marcus — Karthik from Solutions here. Appreciate the doc, Anita — useful. I wanted to lay out the technical tradeoffs and what info we need from Arjun ahead of the workshop so we can keep the call focused.

PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — short guidance - PrivateLink (endpoint services):
  * Pros: no route table changes for your VPCs, minimal blast radius, typically preferred by security teams.
  * Cons: you will provision interface endpoints in each AZ you want low-latency access to; depending on your setup that can be a small operational step.
- VPC Peering:
  * Pros: flat networking, works well if you already run cross-account peering and need high bandwidth between subnets.
  * Cons: requires route table updates and careful CIDR planning to avoid overlap.

Egress model and allowlist - Dedicated NAT per-customer: we can offer a model with a stable, small set of egress IPs dedicated to your tenant for production (recommended if you need tight allowlisting). This will be in the form of a /29 or a small pool depending on scale.
- Shared egress pool: lower operational overhead but requires allowlisting a larger set of IPs — not ideal for payment processors with strict allowlists.

What we need from Arjun before the workshop
1) Preferred topology (PrivateLink preferred? or do you want us to evaluate peering given your existing VPCs)
2) List of subnets/AZs where low-latency connections are required (so we can size endpoint placement)
3) Any proxy termination or TLS interception policies (affects mutual TLS and cert handling)
4) Contact for your cloud infra team if separate from NetOps

I attached an initial, non-final CSV with the candidate Redwood egress IPs we typically propose for Private deployments (redwood-egress-ips-v1.csv). These are placeholders — we will provide a finalized, timestamped list for your firewall team once we lock down deployment topology and scale.

Proposed next step: 45-minute workshop (network + security + infra) — Marcus, can you propose two slots for May 12 (Tue) morning PT?
